title: Design System: 日周报管理系统

display.purpose: Page and panel titles, period labels, auth headlines.

body.purpose: Prose, labels, controls, all UI copy.

label.purpose: Field labels and button text at small sizes.

data.purpose: Dates, day numbers, counts, versions, tokens.

shadows.name: panel-rest
shadows.purpose: Panels rest on hairline borders; depth is tonal.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, colour and border changes.

motion.name: normal
motion.purpose: Modal entrance, slash reveal, row removal.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Top bar + bottom tab bar + week list.

narrative.overview: This is a working record book, not a dashboard. Every day of the month is a cell in a visible, hairline-ruled grid; writing a report means filling a cell, and a weekly or monthly report is that same grid gathered up.
keyCharacteristics: Blueprint ground with white panels; hairline rules do the dividing, not shadows.
One accent — signal blue — for current selection, primary generative action, and the today ring.
Condensed display type for titles and periods; IBM Plex Sans for body; IBM Plex Mono for dates and counts.
Zero-radius calendar cells inside a rounded panel.
A diagonal slash marks actionability and never decorates static content.
Light and dark are the same vocabulary, re-pointed token by token.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal blue means "this is where you are" or "this is the action that produces something". It never fills a surface larger than a button, a row tint, or a 2px line.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: One colour per cadence, used identically in the calendar chip, the summary rail, and the legend: ink for daily, signal for weekly, cyan for monthly.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Report prose is capped at 72ch, always left-aligned under its panel title.

dos: Keep one accent; use weight, size, or a tonal step for emphasis.
Keep dates, counts, versions and identifiers in mono with tabular numerals.
Let hairline rules do the dividing; shadow only for things that float.
Write the action on the button and name the consequence in the confirm dialog.
Keep one component vocabulary across screens.
donts: No coloured side stripe on rows, cards, or alerts.
No nested panels and no card-per-row lists.
No second radius scale, accent hue, or font family for a new screen.
